name: Survey Sense
tagline: Read your home survey like a builder, then negotiate
about: Survey Sense turns a home survey or inspection report into a prioritised defect list with cost bands, explains photos of cracks and damp, and arms you to renegotiate or walk away.
persona: You are a calm building surveyor with a builder's pragmatism: you separate cosmetic from structural, give cost bands not false precision, and say plainly when a specialist is needed.

onboarding.title: Every defect, ranked and priced
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us the property basics so the ranking fits its age and type.
bullets: Photos of cracks and damp explained

tools.title: Decode my survey
tools.subtitle: Paste the report → ranked defects

inputs.label: Paste the report (or the findings section)
inputs.placeholder: Roof: several slipped slates… Damp: high readings to rear wall…

tools.prompt: Decode this survey for the profile's property, agreed price {price}: {report}. Produce a table (Defect | Severity 1–5 | Likely cause | Cost band | Urgency) ordered by severity, bullets of what is normal for a property of this age and type versus what is not, a checklist of specialist reports or quotes to obtain before committing, and a callout on the findings that justify renegotiating or walking away.

tools.title: What's this?
tools.subtitle: Photo of a crack, stain or bulge

inputs.label: Photo of the crack, stain or problem
Where and what you notice
inputs.placeholder: hairline crack above bay window, inside, worse in summer

tools.prompt: Identify what the photo most likely shows given: {where}. Produce a kv (most likely explanation, other possibilities, severity, typical fix, cost band), steps to investigate further yourself safely, bullets of questions for a surveyor or specialist, and a callout on the signs that would make this urgent.

tools.title: Renegotiate the price
tools.subtitle: Turn findings into a number

inputs.label: Key findings and quotes
inputs.placeholder: roof repairs quoted 4,200; damp course 1,800; boiler at end of life

tools.prompt: Findings: {findings}. Agreed price {price} in a {market}. Produce a table (Item | Quoted cost | Ask for | Justification) with a total, text giving the realistic reduction range and what the seller will likely accept, a quote with the exact message to the agent presenting the findings and the revised offer, and a callout on when to accept a partial reduction versus walking away.

tools.title: Which survey do I need?
tools.subtitle: Levels, costs, add-on checks

inputs.label: The property
inputs.placeholder: 1890s terrace with loft conversion and cellar

tools.prompt: Property: {property}, plans: {plans}, region from the profile. Produce a table (Survey level | Covers | Doesn't cover | Typical cost | Best for) of the survey and inspection types available in general terms, text recommending one for this property and why, a checklist of extra specialist checks worth adding (drains, electrics, timber, asbestos, boundaries), and a callout on the difference between a lender's valuation and a survey.

tools.title: Question the surveyor
tools.subtitle: Before the visit or after the report
tools.prompt: Stage: {when}. Worries: {worries}. Produce a checklist of 12 questions to ask the surveyor covering the worries and the profile's property type, bullets on what a vague answer usually means, a quote with a short email requesting clarification, and a callout on what a survey cannot promise in general terms.

disclaimer: General guidance, not a professional survey; structural, electrical, gas and damp issues need a qualified inspector, and all costs are rough estimates.
